locations.name: Entrance & Parking
locations.description: The journey begins at the main entrance off US 190, three miles from downtown Mandeville. Two large parking areas serve the park, and an all-terrain track wheelchair is available for visitor use — ask at the entrance station. Every route in this experience starts here, the way a visitor's real trip does.

locations.name: Accessible Playground
locations.description: Fontainebleau's 7,300-square-foot playground is built for every child: a poured safety surface, accessible ramps, a wheelchair-accessible together glider, tactile roller slide, and inclusive swing seats. It anchors the park's family amenities and sits along the main route from parking to the waterfront.

locations.name: Waterfront Cabins
locations.description: Twelve deluxe cabins overlook Lake Pontchartrain, reopened in late 2024 after a full post-hurricane rebuild — three are ADA compliant, and a larger Lodge sleeps up to ten. The walkway from parking to the cabins is the question every visitor asks first: are there stairs, how wide is the path, can I get there? This experience answers it in first person.

locations.name: Beach & Splash Pad
locations.description: A sandy beach on Lake Pontchartrain, open for swimming year-round, with a seasonal water playground operating Tuesday through Sunday. The route from the parking areas to the sand — surfaces, transitions, and rest points — is captured continuously so visitors can judge their own comfort level before they arrive.

locations.name: Sugar Mill Ruins
locations.description: The brick ruins of Bernard de Marigny's 1829 sugar mill stand near the park entrance — the remnant of the plantation that gave Fontainebleau its name, with interpretive history at the nearby visitor center. A short, level detour from the main route adds the park's story to the journey.
